text:
kevin: Hey team, escalated from a customer — their Go app using the Redwood Go SDK hangs after the first streamed chunk, then the client returns a JSON decoding error: "invalid character '\n' after top-level value". Happening on chunked responses from our hosted API. No obvious error in server logs. Customer says it used to work with an older SDK version.

alyssa: Thanks, kevin. Can you share the Go SDK version and a minimal repro (code + curl)? Also any response headers (Transfer-Encoding, Content-Type) would help.

kevin: Repro snippet from customer (redacted):

```go
resp, err := client.Do(req)
if err != nil { return err }
defer resp.Body.Close()
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
scanner.Split(bufio.ScanLines)
for scanner.Scan() {
    line := scanner.Text()
    var obj map[string]interface{}
    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); err != nil {
        log.Printf("json err: %v, raw=%q", err, line)
        break
    }
    // process obj
}
if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("scan err: %v", err) }
```

They reported using go-sdk v0.3.1; server headers: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. curl -v shows chunks containing parts of JSON objects (i.e., not newline-delimited).

jordan: Two likely culprits: 1) bufio.Scanner defaults to 64KB token limit — it will silently truncate long tokens. 2) the server's chunk boundaries aren't aligned to logical JSON objects; using ScanLines will break framing. For streaming JSON objects, use json.Decoder on the stream: `dec := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body); for dec.More() { var ev Event; if err := dec.Decode(&ev); ... }`. Scanner.Buffer can be increased but Decoder is more robust.

kevin: Tried switching to json.Decoder and larger buffer; that removed the truncation but customer still saw a mid-stream `invalid character` after some bytes. Attached snippet of raw bytes from the log: `...}\n{"event":...` (no delimiter between objects). With Decoder it's fine normally but we still see `EOF` / partial object when the connection gets a 401 mid-stream and server closes.

alyssa: Important detail — did the customer have short-lived auth tokens? If the token expires mid-stream the server can cut the connection and return a 401 HTML/error body, which the Decoder then chokes on. Can you check the access token lifetime and any renewal logs? Also ask them to repro with `-H "Authorization: Bearer <long-lived-token>"` to confirm.

kevin: Confirmed: token TTL is 60s for their test env and the stream lasted ~90s. Logs show a 401 chunked in the middle. Customer sees the JSON decode error because the stream changes to an auth error payload mid-stream.

jordan: That matches. Recommendations: 1) prefer json.Decoder for framing; 2) avoid Scanner for chunked/concatenated JSON; 3) ensure token refresh happens before expiry (token refresh in the client or use a refresh token flow that triggers a reconnect); 4) design the app to handle partial stream closure and reconnect/resume (send last processed event id). Also note we bumped streaming behavior in go-sdk v0.4.0 to better expose reconnect hooks and improved error messages for non-JSON mid-stream payloads.

alyssa: Action items for support: ask customer to try v0.4.0 (we patched decoder usage and added clearer logs), repro with a long-lived token, and attach `curl -v` showing the 401 mid-stream. If they can't upgrade, advise switching to json.Decoder and adding a pre-stream token refresh.

kevin: Will send steps and the patched SDK recommendation. One more question: is there a best-practice for transparent token refresh mid-stream? If the transport layer forces reconnects, we want to avoid event duplication.

jordan: Short answer: no magic server resume header today — app-level resume is safest. Persist the last-seen event id and on reconnect request resume from there. We are exploring resume semantics for future SDKs.

kevin: Great, thanks. I'll follow up with the customer and close if v0.4.0 + token refresh fixes it. :thumbsup:
